summary:
Afyonkarahisar has no distinct legal or policing regime on LGBTI+ matters. The province stands entirely under Turkey's national framework, and the draft omnibus justice package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025 contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific provision. A visitor in the province is subject to the same national statutes, the same identity-document requirements at checkpoints and the same street-level policing practice documented elsewhere in Turkey.

The leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people. Conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, including its so-called promotion, would carry up to three years in prison. Participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies would carry up to four years; because same-sex marriage is not legal in Turkey, such ceremonies are by definition symbolic and any attendance is exposed. Human Rights Watch describes the package as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades.

The same draft restricts gender-affirming care. It would raise the surgery age from 18 to 25 and make permanent infertility mandatory. Medical professionals would face fines or up to seven years for care outside the new limits, and transgender patients up to three years, a combination that would push transition care into underground settings.

Kaos GL's 2025 report, A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy, records six right-to-life violations across the country, three of them logged as hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected. It documents 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the previous year, most linked to peaceful assembly, alongside 336 violations of assembly and 313 violations of liberty. The liberty figure is a roughly 2.5-fold increase made up mostly of detentions, and the report also records event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings.

The counts in that report are drawn from media and civil-society monitoring because the Turkish state keeps no official hate-crime statistics. The report contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific finding; it describes the country-wide framework that governs the province.
tangentialFactors:
Kaos GL situates the 2025 figures within institutionalised hostility: instructions issued under a Year of the Family programme directed at public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events, all described as national practice rather than isolated incidents. The draft package and the reported enforcement pattern therefore reinforce each other, and a visitor should expect the rhetorical framing to be present in official interactions as well as in the statute book.

The absence of official hate-crime statistics is itself a comparative marker. Turkey's documented totals depend on media and civil-society collection, so provincial-level incidents that never reach national reporting cannot be ruled out anywhere in the country, Afyonkarahisar included.
localsOnly:
Residents of Afyonkarahisar are directly exposed to the draft package's penalties as Turkish nationals, including the three-year maximum for conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality and the four-year maximum for participation in same-sex ceremonies. Medical professionals working in the province would fall under the proposed fines and seven-year exposure for care outside the new limits, and transgender patients under the proposed three-year penalty.

The Kaos GL counts describe what Turkish residents have already experienced in 2025: detentions making up most of the 313 liberty violations, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations mostly tied to peaceful assembly, and event-specific bans on gatherings. Because the state records no official hate-crime statistics, residents have no official channel through which such incidents are counted.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted, amended or withdrawn after the 29 October 2025 reporting is not sourced in this inventory; the package is described here as a leaked draft reported at that date.

No Afyonkarahisar-specific enforcement record, detention count, hate-crime figure or provincial police directive is available in the sources reviewed, so the province's actual street-level practice is inferred from the national framework rather than documented locally.

The Kaos GL totals are compiled from media and civil-society reports rather than official statistics, and the report itself contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific finding; the province's share of the recorded violations is unresolved.

Whether the proposed changes to the surgery age, the infertility requirement and the penalties for patients and clinicians would survive legislative scrutiny, and whether any transitional arrangements apply, are not addressed by the sources.
